newsitem.title: USA: High Plains Wheat - Dealers take protection.
newsitem.headline: High Plains Wheat - Dealers take protection.

text.p: Grain dealers in the High Plains were taking widepread three to four cents per bushel protection on hard red winter wheat Monday amid forecasts for a lower opening in KCBT wheat futures.
Dealers said harvest hit high gear over the weekend, and traders in Kansas City said they expected wheat futures to weaken early on harvest pressure.

"They did get a lot cut over the weekend. I came in to the office on Saturday and Sunday and bought several trains (of wheat)," a northern Oklahoma dealer said. "I think the wheat's looking much better than expected."
The dealer said yields in southern Oklahoma were ranging from 25 to 35 bushels per acre (bpa). Fields that were damaged by hail and freeze were showing yields of five to 10 bpa.
Basis values in cents/bu against KCBT wheat, cash=dollars/bu.
(Note: N=KCBT July. unq- unquoted, na - not applicable)
